text:
lina: prototyping a new synthetic load pattern i'm calling "stutter-ramp". goal: combine smooth qps ramps + intermittent microbursts + a tiny fraction of long-sequence injections so kernel selection, batching heuristics, and kv-warmup get exercised in one run. want feedback on phases and measurables.
ben: name is great. can you list the phases and expected observables?
lina: sure — short sketch:
1) warmup (deterministic) to prefill kv and steady state batcher behavior
2) linear ramp from base_qps -> peak_qps over 3 minutes to exercise kernel switching thresholds
3) periodic microstutters (50-300ms, 3-10x) every 20-90s for batching/backpressure
4) long-tail injections: 0.5-2% requests with seq_len > 1024 to force fallback kernels and quant paths
amy: we should use production-derived prefixes for kv prefill (not uniform). otherwise hit-rate profile is unrealistic. also add small ttl jitter to kv entries so eviction windows show up.
raj: ran a quick 10m on the runtime branch. saw p99 jump once seq lengths crossed 512 — looks like kernel auto-selection prefers a slower fallback path for mixed-precision. profiler shows kernel_dispatch +18%, quant_fallback_handler +42%.
ben: we need apples-to-apples comparisons: same seed, same model build, pinned kernel flags vs auto, identical batcher config. compare latency tails, throughput, and kernel choices.
lina: example harness config (pseudo):
```
pattern: stutter-ramp
seed: 1337
warmup: {duration: 120s, mode: replay-seed, kv_prefill: true}
ramp: {start_qps: 60, peak_qps: 2400, duration_s: 180}
stutter: {interval_s: 30, burst_mult: 6, width_ms: 150}
long_tail: {prob: 0.01, seq_len: 1200, prefix_overlap: 0.2}
```
ben: for batching heuristics we should test: fixed-window (e.g., 8ms) vs adaptive (expand if queue_depth > N, contract on slo breaches). record per-request batch_size.
amy: also capture per-token cost and request-level token counts so Optimize can compare unit economics.
raj: small request: when we inject long sequences vary prefix overlap so kv hit-rate toggles from ~80% -> 20% across runs. that helps root-cause cache-vs-kernel interactions.
infra-bot: CI perf job queued: perf-run-stutter-211456 (s3://redwood-ci/load/211456/)
ben: instrumentation: log compact per-request kernel decision (kernel_id, reason: latency|capacity|fallback), batch_size, kv_hit(bool). aggregate to 1s rollups to avoid hot-path pressure.
lina: action items:
- lina: add stutter-ramp generator with seed + ttl-jitter to loadgen (2d)
- amy: implement adaptive-batcher toggle + slo callback in harness (3d)
- raj: rerun profiler with pinned kernel flags and upload flamegraphs (today)
- infra-bot: schedule 1h controlled run on perf-cluster once PRs land
raj: uploaded flamegraphs: s3://redwood-ci/profiles/211456/flamegraphs.tar.gz
ben: plan to produce an apples-to-apples table post-run: p50/p95/p99, median batch_size, kernel distribution, kv-hit-rate, per-token cost.
lina: i'll post the run command here when ready. example: `./loadgen --pattern stutter-ramp --seed 1337 --duration 3600 --profile --out s3://redwood-ci/load/stutter-211456`
amy: heads-up: if runs aren't reproducible double-check the RNG seed, replay mapping, and any nondeterministic time-based TTL jitter settings.
ben: agreed. also capture the chosen kernel per step so we can graph kernel transitions vs seq_len and qps.
infra-bot: perf job started: perf-run-211456 (ETA ~11m)
lina: thanks all. after the run let's sync and inspect p99 clusters and kernel traces.
